correctness.rationale: Projectors onto eigenvalues 0,n-2,n,2(n-1) give every matrix entry exactly. The antipodal/distance-3 entry is h^3(n-2)(n-1)(1-(n-1)h)/6, changing sign once and excluding return. For 0<h<=1/(n-1), all edge entries are h[(1-z)(1+A_m z^2)+z^2/3]>0, all same-part offdiagonal entries have a globally positive quadratic, and diagonal entries are positive because the scalar RK4 stability polynomial is positive on the negative real axis. Intact biclique positivity follows from strictly convex R_4(-z), and the n=3/n>=4 reversal from 8/3<rho<3. Independent exact matrix construction for 10020 entries and three symbolic identities was replayed from actual candidate verify.py. Infinite conclusions rely on the written proof.

originality.rationale: Directly inspected two historical primary full-text journal sources on SSP Runge--Kutta time stepping. residual_risks: A specialized theorem on RK4 positivity in association schemes or bipartite double covers, incompletely indexed or outside the inspected sources, might cover this result; current searches do not prove historical uniqueness.

value.rationale: A complete all-step positivity/no-reentry law on dense diameter-three regular crown graphs establishes that classical RK4 gains no nonnegative-step room over forward Euler while its spectral-stability window is larger by factor rho/2. Deleting a full matching from K_(n,n) counterintuitively lowers the absolute safe RK4 step for every n>=4, although every vertex loses one edge; n=3 is the precise opposite case. Both the exact first-negative entries and sharp graph-size threshold support positivity-sensitive numerical design. This structural graph-operation comparison is not merely an arbitrary invariant or reparameterization.
